title: Renewal & Expansion check-in - Orchard Insurance
next_steps: Send updated pricing for Dedicated + 2 additional regions
Share SOC 2 + ISO docs and network topology guide
Schedule 2-hour benchmark with Orchard infra team w/ sample workload next week
Draft contract amendment for 12-month extension and capacity commit
action_items: Lena Ortiz: Send pricing worksheet and committed capacity options by 2027-11-25
Marcus Chen: Prepare benchmark plan and test harness, target run week of 2027-11-29
Sofie Patel: Share SOC2 report and SSO/SAML integration notes by 2027-11-24
Priya Malhotra: Confirm stakeholders and approve benchmark window by 2027-11-26
summary: Renewal discussion focused on extending contract for 12 months, adding Dedicated capacity (2 more GPU pools) and expanding to EU and APAC regions. Customer concerned about latency for EU/ APAC and data residency; requested SOC2/ISO docs and a benchmark run. AE and SE to send pricing and run benchmarks. Procurement to review contract amendment.
topics: Capacity upgrades - Dedicated GPU pools and burst capacity
Additional regions - EU data residency & APAC latency
Contract extension length and committed spend
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-11-23
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 48 mins
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Sofie Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Malhotra (Orchard CTO), Ben Carter (Orchard Head of ML), Anya Ruiz (Procurement), Daniel Kim (Infra)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone thanks for joining. quick check, can you see my screen?
[00:05] Priya Malhotra: Yep, all good. hi Lena hi Marcus. thanks for setting this up.
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: of course. today's goal is to run through renewal options and the expansion asks - specifically more Dedicated capacity and adding EU and APAC regions, and confirm next steps for the benchmark.
[00:18] Ben Carter: yeah we've been pretty happy overall, latency's been decent on NA but EU users have noticed tail latency spikes. also want to lock in pricing if we extend for 12 months.
[00:27] Marcus Chen: totally - Marcus here. quick note, the tail you've seen is likely from cross-region routing and cold KV cache misses, we can do steady-state tests with prefix caching and warm workers to measure realistic p90/p99.
[00:40] Daniel Kim: and just to flag, Orchards policy requires EU data to stay in region for certain PII pipelines, so if we expand to EU we need region isolation and audited KMS.
[00:50] Lena Ortiz: understood. Redwood Dedicated supports region-specific pools and customer-managed KMS; we'll include the topology doc.
[00:56] Anya Ruiz: procurement question - if we increase committed capacity, what discounts and what happens to overage? do you have a standard amendment?
[01:04] Lena Ortiz: yes we can do tiered committed spend discounting. typical approach is a 12-month extension with reserved GPU pools and overage billed at a lower committed rate, we can attach an amendment. I'll send the worksheet after the call.
[01:15] Priya Malhotra: what about bursting? some months we have peaks around renewals and claims season.
[01:20] Marcus Chen: Dedicated has burst capacity options. performance-wise bursting won't compromise latency SLA if we pre-warm. there is a small delta in cost. we can show sample numbers in the pricing sheet.
[01:30] Ben Carter: we also want APAC region. previous attempts with other providers meant higher token costs. curious how Redwood handles model variants in different regions - is it the same model or a lighter quantized variant?
[01:41] Marcus Chen: good question. we can deploy the same model artifact or a quantized variant in APAC; routing can prefer lower-cost variants but fall back to full model. for regulatory or fidelity-critical pipelines you'd pin full model.
[01:52] Daniel Kim: latency target from our SLAs is p99 < 800ms for chat endpoints in EU and APAC; is that achievable with Dedicated?
[01:59] Marcus Chen: yes, with region-local Dedicated pools plus prefix/KV caching and smarter batching we typically hit p99 in 200-600ms depending on sequence length. we'll validate with your sample payloads.
[02:10] Priya Malhotra: transcription note - sorry we use 'claims' as an umbrella, could be personally identifiable in some flows. KMS and audit logs are non-negotiable.
[02:20] Sofie Patel: we'll include SOC2, ISO and audit logs docs. Marcus will point to the audit log retention options.
[02:27] Anya Ruiz: timeline wise procurement wants to sign by mid-December if numbers look right. can you give a hard date for sending pricing and security docs?
[02:36] Lena Ortiz: yes we can get pricing and security bundle by Friday the 25th. benchmark plan by Monday.
[02:43] Ben Carter: on benchmarks, we care about cold-start vs steady-state. can you simulate our traffic pattern? we can provide logs.
[02:51] Marcus Chen: please share a 24-72 hour sample of traffic patterns, plus prompt templates. we'll run cold-start runs and steady throughput runs and share p50/p90/p99 and token-cost numbers.
[03:02] Daniel Kim: also curious about network egress, is that included or separate? for EU region, egress to our services in EU needs to be minimal.
[03:10] Lena Ortiz: egress is typically billed separately; we'll call out estimated egress costs in the worksheet and suggest colocating your infra if needed.
[03:18] Priya Malhotra: contract amendment — will you support a 12-month renewal with a fixed committed spend and the option to add two more Dedicated pools mid-term?
[03:27] Lena Ortiz: yes we can structure an amendment with an upfront commit and an expansion clause for additional pools with a 30-day notice and rebaseline pricing.
[03:35] Anya Ruiz: is there a minimum notice for adding regions? like EU/APAC - we want to avoid long lead times.
[03:41] Marcus Chen: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks to stand up region capacity depending on GPU availability; with reserved capacity we can shorten that to under a week in many cases.
[03:49] Ben Carter: any gotchas with SAML SSO across regions? we have Okta.
[03:53] Sofie Patel: Okta integrations are standard; the private control plane for Private deployments needs some network config, but for Redwood Dedicated we support SSO and RBAC out of box. we'll send integration notes.
[04:05] Priya Malhotra: security checklist — SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, KMS with HSM support, encrypted at rest and in transit, and fine-grained RBAC. can you confirm all are available?
[04:16] Marcus Chen: yes SOC2/ISO available; KMS integrations with customer-managed keys and HSM are supported in Private and Dedicated; we'll attach certs.
[04:23] Anya Ruiz: also legal needs indemnity language and a data residency clause for EU.
[04:28] Lena Ortiz: we'll loop in legal and propose language; we have standard clauses for EU data residency and can add stricter ones if needed.
[04:35] Priya Malhotra: ok good. on cost tradeoffs, we need guidance — saving tokens vs added latency. do you have any tooling suggestions?
[04:43] Marcus Chen: Redwood Optimize gives model/quantization recommendations and batching suggestions. for your throughput pattern we can model cost vs latency and recommend a config.
[04:51] Ben Carter: can you show us a sample recommendation for our claim summarization pipeline?
[04:55] Marcus Chen: yes we'll include a sample based on your prompt templates in the benchmark.
[05:01] Lena Ortiz: recapping next steps: we'll send pricing + security bundle by 11/25, benchmark plan by 11/29, schedule the benchmark for the week of 11/29, and draft amendment for a 12-month renewal with committed capacity. does that sound right?
[05:13] Priya Malhotra: yes that works; procurement will review on 11/26.
[05:17] Anya Ruiz: please include an explicit line for overage rates and the expansion clause.
[05:21] Lena Ortiz: absolutely.
[05:24] Ben Carter: quick technical clar — when you say prefix caching, do you cache at the token level or KV-level across requests?
[05:30] Marcus Chen: both; we do prefix caching at the request level and manage KV cache for decoder states. some models and quantized runtimes behave slightly different so we'll show the exact config.
[05:42] Daniel Kim: great. for the benchmark we want p99 numbers and a cost per 1M tokens ideally.
[05:48] Marcus Chen: we'll provide p50/p90/p99 and cost per million tokens for both steady-state and cold-start.
[05:54] Priya Malhotra: ok thanks everyone, anything else?
[05:58] Lena Ortiz: one last ask — can you confirm which datasets are considered PII for the legal team, Priya? that'll help scope the EU rules in the amendment.
[06:06] Priya Malhotra: I'll send a short list after the call and cc procurement.
[06:11] Sofie Patel: noted. I'll follow up with SOC2 and SSO notes.
[06:14] Lena Ortiz: perfect. thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the attachments and proposed dates.
[06:18] Priya Malhotra: thanks. bye everyone.

End of transcript.
